Alex — thanks for the quick read. High level responses and proposal below; I attached an annotated eval plan (Redwood-Eval-plan-2026-11.docx) that maps deliverables to pricing triggers.

1) Acceptance criteria for pilot:
- Latency: 95th <= 180ms, 99th <= 350ms (measured across your representative traffic mix, trace window = 48h)
- Error rate: <1% 5xx across same window
- Quality: pass on 3/4 of the supplied prompt set (we'll run blind evals you approve)

If we don't meet the acceptance targets, we commit to a remediation window: 5 business days of joint debugging and a performance replay. If unresolved, we will apply a one-time credit equal to 10% of pilot usage.

2) Availability fallback: we will route traffic to a compatible lower-capacity model in our hosted fleet (latency increase expected) and notify your SREs. We'll include an on-call escalation path in the MAP.

3) Pricing cadence: suggested commercial sequencing —
- Pilot (6 weeks): fixed per-token pilot rate (no overage)
- Post-pilot ramp (months 1–3): committed monthly baseline + volumetric tiers; we propose a 7% discount at 6k qpm committed, 12% at 12k qpm committed.
- Annual commit (signed year): additional 10% strategic discount and priority capacity.

Where the commercial tradeoff comes in: for higher discounts / priority SLAs we need larger committed baseline or a time-bound ramp schedule. We outlined two options in the attached SLA-credit-schedule.pdf — one focused on service credits for SLO misses, the other on upfront rebate-style discounts tied to commit thresholds.

Next step: propose a short sync Thu 11/05 to walk through the MAP and finalize acceptance metrics. Marcus — can you bring the SLA schedule? Ben — can you run the pricing scenarios for 6k vs 12k qpm?

Thanks,
Evelyn
